page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and relies on a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, score in the average tier, while multi-core performance falls into the weak category. Memory bandwidth tests indicate some limitations, with read-only large block bandwidth registering as poor at 15.81 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth as weak at 20.3 GB/sec. However, the CPU's instruction set extensions, including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration like AES and SHA_NI, support tasks like encryption, which achieved average scores in Passmark testing.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the ecs.r7t.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. It is suited for applications such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, text processing, and static web serving, where its 6.4 GB/sec web serving throughput can be leveraged. It is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks, multi-threaded compiling, or large-scale data processing due to its lower multi-core performance and memory bandwidth constraints.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, delivering a high 8.0 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, this KVM-based server includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware acceleration. It does not feature local storage or GPU resources, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average single-core CPU performance and encryption capabilities, contrasted by weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth results. This resource profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for memory-intensive, single-threaded, or moderately demanding workloads. It is best suited for caching, text processing, static web serving, and lightweight database applications that benefit from its high memory-to-vCPU ratio without requiring heavy parallel computation.
